title: Robina — August 2026 Market Overview
notes: Worked example, cut from the 10 real DJI takes (see work/raw_transcript.md). Demonstrates the take-selection the pipeline can't automate away: (1) clip 0060 opens with a repeat of 0026's closing line ('let's jump in') — trimmed. (2) clip 0062 is a 217s take that covers the bridge + median price AND a rough first pass at asking-vs-sale; the asking section is DROPPED because clip 0064 redoes it cleanly. (3) clip 0066 is a discarded first take of the 'new house lending' intro — DROPPED, superseded by the cleaner 0070. (4) clip 0070's tail ('if we click on the three sub average…') is a false start 0076 redoes — trimmed. segments.transcript: Hi there, my name's Will. I sell homes around the Southern Gold Coast, but before I got into real estate, I was a data analyst for many years… so let's jump in.
What we've got here is how long it takes a house to sell in Robina… risen from ~25 days in June to ~50 days now… way above that 10-yr seasonal trend (ex-COVID, rolling 3-mo).
Why does that matter? Days on market is an indicator of buyer demand… but it's a symptom of the current market, not a predictor of where it's headed.

Prices move gradually — appraisals are set off the last 6 months of sales, so asking lags… peak ~$1,500,000 (Mar 2026) now $1,492,000 — a gradual decline, not the magnitude of days-on-market. (DROP the asking-vs-sale portion after this — 0064 redoes it cleanly.)
Clean take: asking sat BELOW sale for most of history → flips ABOVE in Dec 2023 → back to match in Sept 2026. Sellers are adjusting to actually sell.

segments.chapter: Chart 4 · Withdrawn + bridge to leading indicator
segments.transcript: Withdrawn homes: back to pre-GFC, 2022 correction, step up 2021→2023… 2025: 23 unsold vs 2026: 53 already. Trend confirmed. To see AHEAD we need a metric that moves before the market. (Trim the trailing false start at ~1:56.)

New house lending — heavily studied, used by CBA + RBA, strong correlation, moves ~12 months before house prices. (Best take of this intro — 0066 dropped. Trim the 'if we click…' false start at the end.)
Select 3-suburb median, actual timings, all data; marked historical lead/lag pairs → 3-year view: peaked end-2024, halved Q4-2025 (20%) → Q2-2026 (10%). A directional signal, not a certainty.

Three data points, same direction: days-on-market ↑, withdrawals ↑, new-house-lending ↓ (halved). Taken together: flat to declining, very unlikely to be rising — not measures of certainty. (Trim the 'so as I said before, these aren't' restart at ~0:43.)
